instruction: With VLC, play src.mp4 from the desktop and capture the initial 5 seconds; then, use GIMP to turn this segment into an animated GIF and save it as output.gif.

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to use VLC to capture a 5-second clip starting at 00:00 (from the beginning) from src.mp4 and convert it to an animated GIF named output.gif using GIMP. The evaluator checks: (1) file exists at /home/user/Desktop/output.gif, (2) file is a valid GIF format, (3) file size is at least 1KB, (4) GIF has at least 100 frames (for 5-second clip at ~20fps), (5) total duration is approximately 5 seconds (4-6 seconds with tolerance).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts GIF file info including duration calculation by summing frame delays (gimp.py:51-62)
Metric correctly verifies file exists, is valid GIF format, has reasonable file size (>=1KB)
Metric correctly verifies frame count (>=100 frames) appropriate for 5-second clip at ~20fps
Metric correctly verifies duration is approximately 5 seconds (4000-6000ms range with tolerance)
Expected values are semantically correct: min_frames=100, target_duration_ms=5000, min_duration_ms=4000, max_duration_ms=6000
Evaluator provides strong verification of key requirements: file existence, GIF format, frame count, and duration
Minor limitation: Cannot verify clip starts at 00:00 or that content is from src.mp4 (would require video content analysis)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Current implementation is solid and verifies the main requirements effectively
Optional enhancement: Add content-based verification to confirm GIF was created from src.mp4 (advanced feature, not critical)
